R115.note: Self-injected @Lazy proxy routes the internal call through Spring's advice so hasRole('ADMIN') is enforced on the batch path; the ADMIN requirement is the contract the annotation already declared, nothing else changes.

R116.note: setTimeout(recordReminder, delayMs, reminderId, message) removes the string-eval sink entirely and delivers the same two arguments to the same function at the same delay.

R117.note: Passing the raw name with { root: reportsDir } lets send reject '..' with 403; the added typeof guard and error callback only change error-body text (status codes preserved) and are stated, though the write-up misattributes the semantics change to root rather than to the callback.

R118.note: firebase/php-jwt JWT::decode with a pinned HS256 Key closes the forgery, but the catch list omits DomainException, which php-jwt's jsonDecode throws for a structurally 3-part token whose header/payload is not JSON, so garbage tokens that the original handled gracefully now surface as an uncaught exception despite the write-up claiming all malformed-token failures are caught.

R119.note: Secure = true added to the existing CookieOptions; name, value, HttpOnly and Expires unchanged.

R120.note: execFile with an argv array closes the shell injection and the leading-dash guard covers flag injection, but DOMAIN_PATTERN is a new allowlist no stated contract calls for and it rejects legitimate whois queries (IPv6 addresses, AS numbers, bare TLDs, non-punycode IDNs, underscores).

R121.note: @require_POST is the right Django API and brings CsrfViewMiddleware into play, but the existing settings-page <a href> link now gets 405 until a template outside the case is rewritten as a POST form; stated openly as a required follow-up, and a GET-confirm/POST-delete shape would have avoided the break.

R122.note: Building the instance, calling full_clean() and then save() runs the model's validate_file_content magic-byte validator; the Django ValidationError is translated to a DRF 400 with field errors and no legitimate upload is affected.

R123.note: A SHA-256 allowlist from configuration is a sound integrity gate that stops arbitrary bytes executing, but it is a restriction the original did not have (an admin must pre-register every build's hash before upload) and the collectible AssemblyLoadContext.Unload() after Initialize means an approved plugin no longer stays resident to 'extend the application at runtime' as the endpoint's comment describes; both are stated but could stop legitimate plugin use.

R124.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) is DRF's documented pattern and overrides any client-supplied owner without changing other behaviour; note the write-up's claim that a POST without an owner field succeeds is wrong (the ModelSerializer still requires it, exactly as before), and the writable owner field on update is left as an out-of-scope gap.

R125.note: The ast allowlist interpreter with no Call/Attribute/Subscript nodes removes eval and meets the contract for + - * / over names in variables, but _MAX_EXPRESSION_LENGTH = 200 is a length bound the contract does not call for and would reject a long legitimate formula; stated, so 1 not 0.

R126.note: AES via aes.NewCipher with GCM and a random nonce replaces DES-CBC-zero-IV; the 16/24/32-byte key requirement and nonce-prefixed authenticated output are stated and are inherent to swapping the algorithm (any DES key and any DES decryptor had to change regardless), and it also removes the original's panic on non-block-multiple input.
